title: The ward is not a treadmill
memeTop: THE STEP COUNTER SAYS PERSONAL BEST
question: Three days after starting haloperidol, a patient says, 'My legs have subscribed to premium cardio.' He feels intense inner restlessness and keeps pacing, without fever or muscle rigidity. Name the nonselective beta blocker commonly used to relieve antipsychotic-induced akathisia.

partials.relation: Same broad drug class: beta blocker. Propranolol is the intended nonselective agent; class credit does not mean the other drug is an equivalent akathisia treatment.
Correct drug-family concept, but the question asks for a specific medication.

explanation: The restlessness and pacing after an antipsychotic suggest akathisia. Propranolol blocks beta-1 and beta-2 receptors, and placebo-controlled trials support its use for antipsychotic-induced akathisia. Metoprolol is relatively beta-1 selective; benztropine and dantrolene are not beta blockers. The game awards class points for related knowledge, not treatment equivalence.

source.label: Placebo-controlled propranolol trial, British Journal of Psychiatry

title: Spicy food: 1. Esophagus: 0.
memeTop: I CAN HANDLE THE EXTRA HOT SAUCE
memeBottom: THE ESOPHAGUS WOULD LIKE A WORD
question: A student with recurrent reflux calls his latest late-night chili challenge 'a randomized controlled mistake.' His clinician prescribes Prilosec, a proton-pump inhibitor. What is its generic active ingredient?

partials.relation: Same drug class: proton-pump inhibitor, but a different active ingredient.
Related acid-suppression concept; name the specific ingredient in Prilosec for full credit.

explanation: Prilosec contains omeprazole, a proton-pump inhibitor used for acid-related disorders including GERD. Pantoprazole is another PPI, while famotidine is an H2-receptor antagonist. Sharing an indication or drug class earns game partial credit rather than identifying the named product.

title: Bladder notifications: enabled
memeTop: THE PATIENT ASKED FOR MORE STEPS
question: A patient being treated for edema says his bladder has turned on push notifications. The chart lists Lasix, a loop diuretic. Which generic medication is this?

partials.relation: Same drug class: loop diuretic, but a different medication.
Related diuretic knowledge; full credit requires the generic ingredient in Lasix.

explanation: Lasix is the brand name for furosemide, a loop diuretic used for edema. Bumetanide and torsemide are also loop diuretics. Hydrochlorothiazide and spironolactone belong to other diuretic classes; this question identifies a product rather than choosing a treatment regimen.

title: The stairs are the final boss
memeBottom: WHY IS THE BOSS MUSIC PLAYING?
question: A runner with exercise-induced bronchospasm jokes that the stairs have better stamina than he does. His prescribed rescue inhaler is Ventolin HFA. Name its short-acting beta-2 agonist ingredient; either the US or international generic name is accepted.

partials.relation: Same broad short-acting beta-2 agonist family, but not the ingredient in Ventolin HFA.
Related bronchodilator or beta-agonist knowledge; the question asks for the specific Ventolin ingredient.

explanation: Ventolin HFA contains albuterol sulfate. Albuterol is called salbutamol internationally; both names identify the same drug. Levalbuterol is a different active ingredient. Salmeterol is long acting, and ipratropium is an antimuscarinic bronchodilator.

title: Free bedroom carousel
memeTop: ROLLED OVER TO CHECK MY PHONE
question: A patient says rolling over in bed unlocks a free 20-second carousel ride. The Dix-Hallpike maneuver provokes brief vertigo with torsional, upbeating nystagmus; there is no hearing loss or focal neurologic deficit. What is the most likely diagnosis?

partials.relation: Identifies the symptom or a broader vestibular category, but not the full diagnosis.

explanation: Brief position-triggered vertigo with torsional, upbeating nystagmus on Dix-Hallpike testing supports posterior-canal BPPV. A broad answer such as 'vertigo' recognizes the symptom but does not identify its cause.

source.label: AAO-HNS: BPPV clinical practice guideline fact sheet

title: LDL is not a Wi-Fi password
memeTop: THE PATIENT THOUGHT HDL WAS HDMI
memeBottom: WE HAVE A LITTLE COUNSELLING TO DO
question: A patient with high LDL asks whether his cholesterol report needs a software update. His prescription lists Lipitor, an HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor. What is the generic drug?

partials.relation: Same drug class: statin, but a different active ingredient.
Related lipid-lowering knowledge; full credit requires the ingredient in Lipitor.

explanation: Lipitor contains atorvastatin, a statin that inhibits HMG-CoA reductase. Rosuvastatin is another statin. Ezetimibe and fenofibrate lower lipids through different mechanisms.

title: The detector battery was not a spare
memeTop: BORROWED THE ALARM BATTERY FOR THE CONTROLLER
memeBottom: THAT WAS NOT THE SIDE QUEST TO ACCEPT
question: Two nonsmoking roommates develop headache and nausea while a faulty fuel-burning heater runs indoors. One has a conventional pulse-oximeter reading of 99%, but blood co-oximetry shows carboxyhemoglobin of 18%. What is the diagnosis?

partials.relation: Recognizes a broad exposure or hemoglobin problem, but does not identify carbon monoxide.

explanation: Shared symptoms after indoor combustion exposure and elevated carboxyhemoglobin strongly support carbon monoxide poisoning. A conventional two-wavelength pulse oximeter can appear reassuring because it cannot reliably distinguish carboxyhemoglobin from oxyhemoglobin.

source.label: CDC: Clinical guidance for carbon monoxide poisoning

title: Free pizza, expensive gravity
memeBottom: BLOOD PRESSURE DID NOT GET THE MEMO
question: A patient stands quickly when someone announces free pizza and becomes lightheaded. After five minutes supine, BP is 128/78 mmHg; after one minute standing it is 102/64 mmHg, and at three minutes it remains 104/64 mmHg. What finding explains the dizziness?

partials.relation: Recognizes the pressure change, but omits its specific relationship to standing.

explanation: The systolic pressure falls by 26 mmHg and the diastolic pressure by 14 mmHg after standing. This meets the usual orthostatic threshold of at least a 20-mmHg systolic or 10-mmHg diastolic fall within three minutes. The numbers identify the finding; the underlying cause still needs assessment.

source.label: CDC STEADI: Measuring orthostatic blood pressure
